analysis: Examined the new .github/workflows/ci-dev-hourly.yml (lines 1-38), the changelog fragment, and the docs/developer/build.md additions (patch hunk at head lines ~337-356). The workflow is a cron/workflow_dispatch job on ubuntu-24.04 with top-level permissions {} and job-level actions: write, contents: read. It does not check out code and has no untrusted inputs: GH_TOKEN is github.token and REPOSITORY is github.repository, both passed through env, not interpolated into the script. The script only queries ci-dev.yml runs on dev and dispatches ci-dev.yml with --ref dev. No PR-controlled data, secrets, or artifacts flow into the job. The only concern is token scope: actions: write can dispatch workflows and cancel runs, and it is limited to a short-lived GITHUB_TOKEN with no checkout, so the risk is minimal. Impact on the threat model: the change touches only CI scheduling. It does not touch provider code, coordinator contract, attestation, keys, cache storage, or release signing, so none of the TB-002/003/007/009/011-014 assets or threats (including T-041) are affected. The doc changes are descriptive. One integration note, not a finding: the workflow depends on dev's ci-dev.yml accepting workflow_dispatch and selecting all components, and on a failure-reporting issue. Neither is in the supplied evidence, so it is unverified. The consequence is only an HTTP 422 on the hourly job, an availability or CI-coverage issue, not a security regression. Dispatched runs on dev may use Darkbloom routing or the Blacksmith fallback, but cache saves only happen on push events, so scheduled runs do not extend cache poisoning. Release workflows are unaffected.
